column5: Not a duplicate (passing mentions only in persian-empire, peloponnesian-war-city-states, herodotus-inquiry-method). Core Idea dated the wars "499–479 BCE" as if that were the whole span; standard references run them to 449 BCE (Wikipedia 499–449; Britannica 492–449), so marked 499–479 as the main phase. Checked: Ionian Revolt 499, Lade/Miletus 494, Athens+Eretria aid, Marathon 490 with Plataeans, Xerxes 480, Plataea and Mycale 479, Laurium silver/Themistocles fleet, Herodotus army ~2.5 million (modern ~200,000): en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greco-Persian_Wars. Thermopylae ~7,000 Greeks, 300 Spartans, rearguard ~2,000 incl. 700 Thespians, 400 Thebans: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Thermopylae, worldhistory.org. 31 states on the Serpent Column ("about thirty"): en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serpent_Column. Delian League 478, treasury in temple of Apollo on Delos: britannica.com/event/Delian-League. Pheidippides Athens-Sparta (Hdt 6.105-6); Marathon-Athens run in Plutarch and Lucian: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pheidippides. Alexander 330s, Peloponnesian War 431: standard. Hard prereqs formal-systems; ok.

Not a duplicate (no other file mentions Maurya, Ashoka or Gupta; physics hit is Gupta-Bleuler). Maurya c. 321-185 BCE, Chandragupta took Magadha/Pataliputra, Ashoka third emperor and grandson, reign 268-232, Kalinga on Bay of Bengal coast, Megasthenes sent by Seleucus I, Arthashastra authorship/date debated: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurya_Empire. Edicts mostly Prakrit in Brahmi (Kharoshthi in NW, a few Greek/Aramaic), "earliest written and datable texts from India", courtesy to Brahmanas and Sramanas: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edicts_of_Ashoka. Rock Edict XII tolerance, Mahinda mission to Sri Lanka: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_Rock_Edicts, Mahinda_(Buddhist_monk). Chandragupta I c. 319/320, Samudragupta, Chandragupta II, tributary states, Kalidasa at Chandragupta II's court, Faxian 399-411, Skandagupta vs Huna c. 455, Nalanda under Kumaragupta I, collapse 6th c.: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gupta_Empire. Aryabhata b. 476 (from Aryabhatiya, 499 at age 23): britannica.com Aryabhata-I. Alexander at Indus 326 BCE: standard. Prereqs all soft and exist; ok.

Not a duplicate (Constantine hits elsewhere are the Donation-of-Constantine forgery and art history; byzantine-orthodox-christianity starts later). Great Persecution from Feb 303, traditionally ended with Edict of Milan 313 (Constantine + Licinius), Decius 249-251 universal sacrifice order, Valerian 257-258: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diocletianic_Persecution. Edict of Thessalonica 27 Feb 380 (Nicene state church), sacrifice bans 391-392: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edict_of_Thessalonica, penelope.uchicago.edu Encyclopaedia Romana. Pauline letters from c. 50 CE, earliest Christian texts: britannica.com/topic/Pauline-letters. Tacitus Ann. 15.44 Nero/fire 64, Christus executed under Pilate (Tiberius): en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tacitus_on_Jesus, livius.org. Milvian Bridge 28 Oct 312, Nicaea 325 on Arian dispute: historytoday.com, britannica Constantine list. Pliny-Trajan letters and imperial cult from Augustus: standard. Hard prereq formal-systems; all prereqs exist; ok.

Not a duplicate (only art-history mesoamerican-and-pre-columbian-visual-expression and an anthropology mention). Core Idea defined Mesoamerica as "central Mexico to Honduras"; the standard definition runs to Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica (Kirchhoff; worldatlas.com/regions/mesoamerica, Wikipedia Mesoamerica). Fixed. Checked: Classic 250-900, Yucatan/Guatemala/Belize, k'uhul ajaw divine kingship, bloodletting, decipherment from the 1950s (Knorozov, Proskouriakoff), Long Count, zero, 9th-c. southern collapse with warfare/drought/environment, Chichen Itza major northern city after the south declined, Tikal-Calakmul rivalry, >6 million Maya today, Spanish contact 1511-1546: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maya_civilization. Olmec Gulf Coast (Veracruz/Tabasco), San Lorenzo then La Venta (~900 BCE), basalt heads from the Tuxtlas ~60 km, "mother culture" debate: people.wku.edu Olmec notes, Wikipedia Olmec colossal heads. 1200-400 BCE is the usual textbook range (Wikipedia gives c. 1600-350 overall). 2012 = end of b'ak'tun 13; Palenque projects to 4772 CE: Lounsbury (precolumbia.org). Maize/beans/squash: standard. Prereqs all soft and exist; ok.

Not a duplicate (Egypt topics mention Nubia only as an Egyptian frontier). Kush: 25th Dynasty 754-656 BC ("over a century"), Piye takes Lower Egypt c. 727, Taharqa, Assyrian invasion 671 and expulsion by 663-656, temple restoration, capital to Meroe (Aspelta), Meroe iron ore/hardwood/slag, kandakes, steep pyramids, Meroitic script readable but language poorly understood, end c. 350 AD: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Kush. Aksum: 1st c. AD, Eritrea/northern Ethiopia, Adulis, ivory/gold exports, gold/silver/bronze coins with Greek legends, stelae, Mani's four great kingdoms (Kephalaia, end of 3rd c.), Ezana c. 330s with Frumentius, cross replaces disc and crescent, Ge'ez, refuge for Muslims 615, decline from 7th c. with Red Sea changes: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Aksum. "One of the first states to adopt Christianity" (after Armenia 301) is the usual framing. Prereqs all soft and exist; ok.

Not a duplicate: conquistador-conquest-colonization and spanish-colonial-empire treat the conquest and colony, not the pre-conquest tribute empire. Tenochtitlan 1325 on island in Lake Texcoco (eagle on cactus), Triple Alliance 1428 with Texcoco/Tlacopan after defeating Azcapotzalco, hegemonic/indirect tribute rule with local rulers kept, Cortés ~530-630 men 1519, Tlaxcalan allies (up to ~100,000 Indigenous warriors), Moctezuma died 1520 in Spanish custody, smallpox 1520, fall 13 Aug 1521: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aztec_Empire. Templo Mayor twin shrines Huitzilopochtli/Tlaloc: worldhistory.org/Templo_Mayor. Population 100,000-200,000+ (Britannica Mexico City history), aqueduct from Chapultepec, causeways, Tlatelolco market: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenochtitlan. Quetzalcoatl-return story post-conquest (Gomara 1552, Florentine Codex), doubted by Townsend, AHR 108:3 (2003): en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_gods. Codex Mendoza mid-1500s (c. 1541) and chinampas: standard. Prereqs all soft and exist; ok.

Not a duplicate (only passing mentions in conquistador-conquest-colonization, spanish-colonial-empire, decolonizing methods). Tawantinsuyu "four parts", largest pre-Columbian empire, Ecuador to central Chile, Pachacuti 1438, Topa Inca north/south expansion, Huayna Capac in Ecuador, no money/markets, no developed writing, mit'a, quipus, Inti/son of the Sun, Machu Picchu as Pachacuti estate, Huayna Capac d. 1520s probably epidemic, civil war 1529-32, 168 Spaniards at Cajamarca, execution 29 Aug 1533, Vilcabamba to 1572: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inca_Empire. Cajamarca 15/16 Nov 1532: britannica.com/event/Battle-of-Cajamarca-1532. Roads ~40,000 km, chasqui relays, tambos: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inca_road_system. Coricancha gold sheets: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coricancha. Lima 1535 and Tupac Amaru II 1780-81: britannica.com Peru. Mitmaq resettlement and freeze-dried potatoes: standard. Prereqs all soft and exist; ok.

Partial overlap: economic-social-history/ancient-trade-networks has one question on the Indian Ocean network and literature/swahili-literature-coastal-merchant-culture covers Swahili writing, but no history topic covers the 1200-1450 network, Swahili city-states or Zheng He; judged a real gap. Monsoon SW in summer / NE in winter, Gujarat-East Africa season Nov-Apr, compass from China: Cambridge "Geography of the Indian Ocean and its navigation" intro (doi 10.1017/9781108341004.002), LibreTexts 2.03 Trade and Interaction in the Indian Ocean. Ibn Battuta at Kilwa 1331 ("one of the most beautiful and well-constructed towns"): en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilwa_Kisiwani, whc.unesco.org/en/list/144. Zheng He voyages to Malindi (6th-7th), seven voyages 1405-1433, Vasco da Gama Calicut 1498: Wikipedia Malindi Kingdom, standard. Swahili as Bantu with Arabic loans, coral-stone mosques, Zimbabwe-plateau gold, Kilwa/Mombasa/Aden/Hormuz/Calicut/Malacca, goods by region: standard (AP World 2.3, OER Project). Prereqs all soft and exist; ok.

Not a duplicate (no other file mentions the sultanate). Explainer said Alauddin fought the Mongols "around 1300, when Mongol armies were conquering much of Asia"; by then the empire had split and the raids came from the Chagatai Khanate (1297-1306: Wikipedia Mongol invasions of India 1297-98, 1303, 1306; Battle of Kili). Reworded. Checked: 1206-1526, five dynasties Mamluk/Khalji/Tughlaq/Sayyid/Lodi, 2nd Tarain 1192 vs Prithviraj Chauhan, Muhammad of Ghor d. 1206, Aibak a former slave, Razia 1236-40, Muhammad bin Tughluq c. 1325-51 with Daulatabad, token currency and greatest extent, Timur sack Dec 1398, Persian official, jizya, Hindu officials and revenue elites, Qutb Minar begun by Aibak, Panipat 21 Apr 1526 vs Ibrahim Lodi: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi_Sultanate. Ibn Battuta qadi of Delhi under Muhammad bin Tughluq: britannica.com/biography/Ibn-Battuta. Vijayanagara 1336 (Harihara, Bukka): britannica.com India Vijayanagar empire. Babur from Timur (father) and Chinggis (mother): standard. Hard prereq rise-of-islam formal-systems; ok.

Not a duplicate (only an art-history mention). 1501-1736 (Isfahan falls 1722, Nader Shah 1736), Twelver Shi'ism imposed on a largely Sunni population, Ardabil Sufi order, Qizilbash "red heads" Turkic tribes, Abbas I 1588-1629 curbing Qizilbash, ghulams from Georgia/Armenia/Circassia, capital to Isfahan 1598, Armenian deportations and silk, Persian administration: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safavid_Iran. Ulama imported from Jabal Amil: Abisaab, Iranian Studies (cambridge.org), Wikipedia Safavid conversion of Iran. Chaldiran 23 Aug 1514, Selim I, artillery and Janissary firearms, eastern Anatolia taken: britannica.com/event/Battle-of-Chaldiran. Tabriz 1501, Hormuz 1622 with English ships, Kandahar disputed with Mughals (1622, 1649): Wikipedia Portuguese-Safavid wars, Mughal-Persian wars. Naqsh-e Jahan square, New Julfa: standard. Hard prereq formal-systems; ok.

Not a duplicate: medieval-japan stops at 1600; literature/edo-period-literature-popular-culture covers literature only. Explainer said Chinese merchants traded "there" (on Dejima); they traded at Nagasaki, confined from 1689 to the walled Tojin yashiki, not Dejima (city.nagasaki.lg.jp Tojin-yashiki documents, samurai-archives Tojin yashiki). Reworded. Checked: Sekigahara 1600, shogun 1603, Yoshinobu resigns 1868, ~270 han ("some 250" ok), sankin-kotai with families in Edo, Christianity banned 1614, 1635 seclusion edicts, Dutch at Dejima, shogunal control of Osaka/Nagasaki and mines, official four-status order, Edo >1 million, Perry 1853 and Kanagawa 1854: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokugawa_shogunate. Shimabara 1637-38, Portuguese expelled 1639: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shimabara_Rebellion. Korea/Ryukyu/Ainu via Tsushima/Satsuma/Matsumae, sakoku a later coinage, Basho, Rangaku: standard. Hard prereq medieval-japan formal-systems; ok.

Not a duplicate (only a passing mention in voltaire-enlightenment-religious-critique). Ivan IV crowned 1547, Kazan 1552, Astrakhan 1556, Yermak 1581, Time of Troubles, Michael Romanov chosen by Zemsky Sobor 1613, 1649 Ulozhenie, Peter co-tsar 1682, empire 1721, Ivan III's 1472 marriage to Sophia: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tsardom_of_Russia. Ivan III 1462-1505, Novgorod 1478, Ugra 1480, Sophia niece of Constantine XI: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_III_of_Russia, britannica Rurikid Muscovy. Moskvitin reached Sea of Okhotsk 1639: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Moskvitin. Table of Ranks 1722, beard tax 1698, Holy Synod 1721, Grand Embassy shipyards: worldhistory.org/article/2304. Pugachev 1773-75 and noble privileges (1785 Charter): en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pugachev's_Rebellion. Crimea 1783, partitions with Prussia/Austria, Anhalt-Zerbst princess: britannica Russia reign of Catherine II, Lumen. Poltava 1709, St Petersburg 1703, Great Northern War 1700-21, emancipation 1861, Voltaire/Diderot correspondence, "Third Rome", tsar from caesar: standard. Prereqs all soft and exist; ok.

Not a duplicate (only literature/puritan-and-colonial-american-literature and an archaeology mention). House of Burgesses Jul-Aug 1619 first elected assembly, ~20 Africans Aug 1619 (White Lion), Rolfe tobacco c. 1611-12, 1662 partus sequitur ventrem: home.nps.gov/jame African Americans at Jamestown, blackpast.org Evolution of Slavery in Virginia. King Philip's War 1675-76, Metacom/Wampanoag, deadliest per capita: history.com King Philip's War, estuarymagazine.com. Winthrop "city upon a hill" 1630: billofrightsinstitute.org, worldhistory.org/article/1660. Bacon's Rebellion 1676 and shift to enslaved labor: courses.lumenlearning.com wm-ushistory1. New Netherland taken 1664, Penn charter 1681, Georgia charter 1732: LibreTexts Locks ch. 5 chronology, georgiahistory.com. Jamestown 1607 Virginia Company, Powhatan, Plymouth 1620 Separatists, Williams/Hutchinson banished, Navigation Acts, 1763: standard. Prereqs all soft and exist; ok.

Not a duplicate (political-science separation-of-powers and legislative-branch-systems mention the Convention only in passing). Explainer said Madison "guided ten amendments through Congress"; Congress proposed twelve on 25 Sep 1789 and ten were ratified 15 Dec 1791 (archives.gov/founding-docs/bill-of-rights-transcript, archivesfoundation.org Original 12 Amendments). Reworded. Checked: Articles adopted 15 Nov 1777, in force 1 Mar 1781 (Wikipedia Articles of Confederation, shmoop timeline); twelve states, Rhode Island absent, Washington presiding, May-Sep 1787 (history.com 7 things, csac.history.wisc.edu); New Hampshire ninth 21 Jun 1788 (EBSCO, history.com); Shays 1786-87, Northwest Ordinance 1787, three-fifths for representation and direct taxes, 1808 import clause (battlefields.org Shays' Rebellion; Art. I §§2, 9). Virginia/New Jersey Plans, Great Compromise, Federalist authors, Art. VII nine states, signed 17 Sep 1787: standard. Hard prereq american-revolution formal-systems; ok.

Not a duplicate (french-revolution-origins gives Napoleon one paragraph; no other Napoleon file). Explainer listed Britain among the armies that won at Leipzig; the field armies were Russian, Prussian, Austrian and Swedish, with only a British rocket unit (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Leipzig). Reworded to Britain as funder/member of the coalition. Checked: 18 Brumaire 9 Nov 1799, First Consul, Concordat 15 Jul 1801, slavery law 20 May 1802 and decrees for Guadeloupe/Guiana, Berlin Decree 21 Nov 1806: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reinstatement_of_slavery_by_Napoleon, Berlin_Decree. 1812 army 450,000-685,000, summer losses to typhus/desertion, Moscow fire: history.com, education.nationalgeographic.org. Height ~1.69 m, French vs English inches, British caricature: scienceabc.com (Tim Clayton). 1794 abolition, coronation 1804, Civil Code 1804, Austerlitz 1805, Trafalgar 1805, HRE ended 1806, Joseph/Louis/Murat thrones, Peninsular War 1808, abdication 1814, Elba, Waterloo June 1815, St Helena 1821, Haiti 1804: standard. Hard prereq formal-systems; ok.

Not a duplicate (only an economics mention). Bayonne 1808 and Joseph as king, juntas from Apr 1810 in Ferdinand's name, Ferdinand's 1814 restoration, Hidalgo executed 1811: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_American_wars_of_independence (its infobox runs to 1833; 1808-1826 is the usual textbook span ending with Callao). Boyaca 7 Aug 1819, Ayacucho 9 Dec 1824 under Sucre, Andes crossing/Chacabuco 1817, Plan of Iguala 1821 Iturbide: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Ayacucho, Battle_of_Boyaca, britannica Latin America culmination of independence. Court to Rio 1808, Joao VI home 1821, Pedro declares independence 7 Sep 1822 and emperor, Lei Aurea 1888, republic 1889: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_of_Brazil, Transfer_of_the_Portuguese_court_to_Brazil. Casta hierarchy, Creole leadership, caudillos, Gran Colombia breakup: standard. Hard prereq spanish-colonial-empire formal-systems; ok.

Not a duplicate (cotton-economy-slavery and historiography topics mention the war in passing). Deaths ~620,000 (old) to ~750,000 (Hacker 2011): discovere.binghamton.edu, history.com Bob Zeller. Union ~22 million incl. border states, Confederacy ~9.1 million with ~3.5 million enslaved: census.gov history April 2015, historyofwar.org population map. ~179,000 Black soldiers (~10% of Union Army): home.nps.gov/chyo African Americans in the Civil War. SC secession 20 Dec 1860 and six more within 40 days: scencyclopedia.org, Wikipedia Presidential transition of Abraham Lincoln. Dred Scott 1857 (no citizenship, no congressional ban in territories): en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dred_Scott_v._Sandford, nps.gov timeline. Fort Sumter 12 Apr 1861, 13th Amendment ratified Dec 1865: law.cornell.edu Amdt13.2. Missouri Compromise 1820, Compromise of 1850, Kansas-Nebraska 1854, Harpers Ferry 1859, Antietam Sep 1862, EP 1 Jan 1863 excluding border states, Gettysburg/Vicksburg July 1863, Atlanta and March to the Sea 1864, Appomattox 9 Apr 1865, Lincoln shot 14 Apr: standard. Prereqs all soft and exist; ok.

Not a duplicate (abolition-movement mentions the Freedmen's Bureau in passing; no Reconstruction topic). Freedmen's Bureau 1865, Black Codes 1865-66, Civil Rights Act 1866 over veto, 14th 1868, Reconstruction Acts 1867 five military districts, impeachment 1868 and one-vote acquittal, 15th 1870, Revels 1870 and Bruce, first public school systems, Field Order 15 reversed by Johnson, KKK and Enforcement Acts, Panic of 1873, Compromise of 1877 and troop withdrawal, Dunning School vs later historians: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reconstruction_era. ~4 million freedpeople, sharecropping, poll taxes and literacy tests, Plessy v. Ferguson 1896: standard. Hard prereq american-civil-war formal-systems; ok.

Not a duplicate (only passing mentions in economic-history topics). 3 Jan 1868 restoration, Satsuma-Choshu alliance 1866, young Mutsuhito, Boshin War, Charter Oath: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meiji_Restoration. Han to prefectures 1871, conscription 1873, monetary land tax 1873, stipends commuted 1876, Haito Edict 1876: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haito_Edict, britannica Empire of Japan emergence of modern Japan, newworldencyclopedia Meiji period. Shimbashi-Yokohama 1872, Tomioka 1872: japantimes.co.jp 2022 rail 150th, Wikipedia Tomioka Silk Mill. Constitution 11 Feb 1889 on Prussian lines, franchise ~1% (15 yen): laits.utexas.edu Meiji Politics. Extraterritoriality ended 1899, tariff autonomy 1911, Iwakura Mission 1871-73: researchonline.lse.ac.uk/6899, foreignaffairs.com. Army French then Prussian (Meckel 1885), navy British: Wikipedia Jakob Meckel, globalsecurity.org. Charter Oath clause, Satsuma Rebellion 1877, Shimonoseki 1895/Taiwan, Korea 1910: ocw.mit.edu 21H.154 lec20, newworldencyclopedia. Fukoku kyohei, zaibatsu, education 1872, Russo-Japanese War: standard. Hard prereq tokugawa-japan formal-systems; ok.

Not a duplicate (only a passing mention in economic-social-history/factory-system-labor). Explainer credited Wisconsin with leading states in the initiative, referendum and recall; Wisconsin led on the direct primary (first statewide primary 1903), while the "Oregon System" pioneered initiative/referendum (1902) and recall (1908) (sos.oregon.gov Blue Book history, EBSCO Expansion of direct democracy). Reworded. Checked: Riis 1890, Tarbell's Standard Oil series, TR's "muckrake" speech 1906 (spartacus-educational, encyclopedia.com Muckrakers); Jungle and both food laws 30 Jun 1906 (Wikipedia Pure Food and Drug Act, britannica Meat Inspection Act); Hull House Sep 1889 Addams/Starr (britannica Hull-House); Triangle fire 25 Mar 1911, 146 dead, locked doors, Factory Investigating Commission (EBSCO, AFL-CIO); TR ~230 million acres (home.nps.gov/thro); Wilson segregation of federal offices, NAACP 1909 (woodrowwilsonhouse.org, whitehousehistory.org); 16th Feb 1913, 17th Apr 1913, 18th Jan 1919, 19th Aug 1920 (govinfo HMAN-117). Fed Reserve Act 1913, Clayton and FTC 1914, Wells anti-lynching, eugenics/immigration restriction: standard. Prereqs all soft and exist; ok.

Not a duplicate (no other topic covers it). Diaz 1876-1911, Madero jailed and calls revolt 1910, Diaz resigns May 1911, Zapata in Morelos, Huerta coup Feb 1913 and Madero killed, Carranza's Constitutionalists beat Huerta then Villa by 1915, 1917 Constitution, Carranza killed 1920, party of 1929 ruling to 2000: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Revolution. Plan of Ayala Nov 1911, Veracruz Apr-Nov 1914, Columbus raid 9 Mar 1916 and Pershing expedition failing to catch Villa: britannica.com Mexican Revolution (Huerta and US intervention), latinamericanstudies.org chronology. Articles 3/27/123 (secular schooling, national subsoil ownership, eight-hour day and right to strike): sjsu.edu Watkins PEMEX, modeldiplomat glossary. Cardenas 1934-40, ejidos, oil expropriation 18 Mar 1938: history.state.gov/milestones/1937-1945/mexican-oil. Celaya 1915, Zapata killed 1919, Obregon president 1920: standard. Prereqs all soft and exist; ok.

Not a duplicate (only passing comparisons in civil-rights topics). Core Idea called 1948 a "whites-only election"; qualified Coloured men in the Cape were still on the common roll until 1956, and 1958 was the first whites-only electorate (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apartheid_legislation, Coloured_vote_constitutional_crisis, sahistory.org.za). Matched the Explainer's "nearly all voters were white". Checked: Population Registration and Group Areas Acts 1950, Natives Land Act 1913 (<1/10 of land), homelands not recognized (Wikipedia Apartheid legislation, Natives Land Act); Sharpeville 21 Mar 1960, 69 dead, emergency, ANC/PAC banned; MK 1961; Rivonia life sentences June 1964 for sabotage (sahistory.org.za, facinghistory.org); Soweto 16 Jun 1976 Afrikaans (Wikipedia Soweto uprising); unbanning 2 Feb 1990, release 11 Feb 1990 (nelsonmandela.org, Wikipedia 1990 opening speech); Freedom Charter 26 Jun 1955 Kliptown; ~3.5 million removed (Surplus People Project, csmonitor 1983); Bantu Education Act 1953 (britannica). Union 1910, ANC 1912, Mixed Marriages Act, 1980s emergencies and sanctions, April 1994, TRC under Tutu: standard. Prereqs all soft and exist; ok.

Not a duplicate (social-science IR topics mention the EU in passing; music hits are "Schumann"). Schuman Declaration 9 May 1950, ECSC (Treaty of Paris 1951, six members), Rome 1957 EEC, 1973 UK/Ireland/Denmark, Greece 1981, Spain/Portugal 1986, Single European Act 1986, Maastricht in force 1 Nov 1993, euro 1999/2002, ten members 2004, Bulgaria/Romania 2007, Croatia 2013, EP direct elections 1979, eurozone crisis, Brexit referendum 2016 and exit 31 Jan 2020: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_European_Union. Non-euro members Denmark (opt-out), Sweden, Poland, Czechia, Hungary, Romania as of 2026: mappr.co currency map 2026, aljazeera.com 2025-12-30. Monnet's role, customs union/CAP, Marshall Plan encouraging cooperation, 8 of 10 2004 entrants ex-communist: standard. Prereqs all soft and exist; ok.
